title: Advertising Signs, Tax Disputes, and City Works
summary:
*   **Tax Assessments Corrected:** The City Council canceled multiple property tax assessments for "credits" after owners, like Henry Oertli Jr. and W.P. Allen, provided affidavits stating they did not possess the taxable assets.
*   **Advertising Sign Permit Revoked:** A permit for a large steel advertising sign near Congress Avenue was granted, then its location changed, and ultimately revoked entirely after strong protests from the building's property owner.
*   **Public Works and Budget Adjustments:** Contracts were awarded for a new cemetery fence and a concrete pier at the city dam. The council also made several internal budget transfers and appropriations, including funds for the City Hospital, Fire Department, and Police Department.
*   **Judicial Fairness:** A $25 fine for abusive language was reduced to $5 following a recommendation from the Corporation Court Judge, who deemed the original amount excessive and possibly erroneous.

October 28th 1914.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Whereas, it has been made
known to the City Council by Mr Elbert M Jones, whose Mother owns the premises at the
southeast corner of the intersection of East 6th street with Brazos street in this City ,
that his Mother has not heretofore consented ,nor does she now consent ,and is extremely
opposed to the placing of a large size electric light sign by the Stires Outdoor
Advertising Co upon the wall over her building at the corner of 6th street and Brazos
street in this City; and Whereas, the City Council issued a permit on October 27th 1914,
to the Stires Outdoor Advertising Company to place a large size electric light sign over
the building at the southeast corner of east 6th street at its intersection with Brazos
street in this City under the impression that the owners and occupants of the building
over which the sign was to be erected had consented thereto,but as it now appears to be
otherwise. Now, therefore, Resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That, in
consideration of the premises hereof and the strong protest made by Mr Elbert M Jones,
agent for his Mother, the owner of said building ,upon the top of which said steel sign 10
X 30 feet was to have been erected by the Stires Outdoor Advertising Co, against the
erection of said sign ,the permit heretofore issued by the City Council, to-wit, on the
27th day of October 1914, to erect and maintain said sign, is hereby cancelled and revoked
.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 4
Nay Councilman Anthony 1
